captions.text: Welcome to this documentary about the history of computing.
We'll explore how computers evolved from room-sized machines to devices in our pockets.
The story begins in the 1940s with the first electronic computers.
ENIAC, developed at the University of Pennsylvania, weighed 30 tons.
It performed 5,000 calculations per second, an incredible feat for its time.
The transistor revolution of the 1950s changed everything.
Small, reliable, and efficient, transistors replaced vacuum tubes.
This paved the way for the modern computer age.
